deities: Sri Trikoteswara Swamy (Shiva, lingam form; on Brahma Shikharam)
festivals: Maha Shivaratri (major annual festival drawing lakhs)

history.dynasty: Chola (inscriptions); Vijayanagara-era patrons; later Zamindari additions
history.period: Existed before 1172 CE (inscriptions of late Chola king Kulothunga Chola and feudatory Muranginayu); present main shrine built 1761
history.summary: CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV says 'Guntur' but the temple is at Kotappakonda village in Narasaraopet mandal, Palnadu district (carved out of the former Guntur district) - documented with the corrected location. A Shaiva hill temple on Trikutadri ('hill of three peaks'), whose three summits - Brahma, Rudra and Vishnu Shikharams - are said to represent the Trimurti and are visible from every direction. Legend: devotee Anandavalli (Gollabhama) performed penance on Rudra hill; Shiva followed her home as Jangama Deva and turned into the lingam that became the new (Paata Kotayya) shrine, then 'relocated' to Brahma Shikharam. Inscriptions confirm existence before 1172 AD; Krishnadevaraya and Vijayanagara kings gifted lands; the present main temple was built in 1761 by Narasaraopet zamindar Raja Malraju Narasimha Rayulu. The hill is 1,587 ft; the main shrine stands at about 600 ft, reached by steps (sources cite 750 and 1,000 - verify) and a motorable road. Dravidian style with gopurams, mandapams and a tiered vimana; holy ponds on the hill including Papanasa Teertha.

name: Kotappakonda Trikoteswara Swamy Temple
town: Kotappakonda (CSV town 'Guntur' is imprecise - Guntur is the old district town; actual location is Kotappakonda village near Narasaraopet, Palnadu district)
town_description: Kotappakonda is a village in Narasaraopet mandal of Palnadu district, Andhra Pradesh, dominated by the three-peaked Trikutadri hill visible for miles around. A year-round Shaiva pilgrimage centre, it becomes a massive congregation point during Maha Shivaratri. Narasaraopet (~17 km) is the nearest rail and market town.

travel.road: Motorable road to the hill plus stepped pathway to the summit; RTC buses connect Narasaraopeta (~17.7 km).

visitor_information.best_time: October to February (cooler); Maha Shivaratri (Feb/Mar) is the peak festival with very heavy crowds.
visitor_information.opening_hours: 5:30 AM-1:30 PM and 3:00-9:00 PM (per velpu/templetimings - verify).
